💰 Build the Seller Profit Cowork Plugin

Connect a public MCP server to Cowork with WIQD, a connector and a custom skill, then let Cowork act as a profitability advisor.

🎯 What we will build

In this lab you build a small Cowork plugin with WIQD. It has two parts: a skill that tells Cowork how to think about seller profitability, and a connector to the public Seller Profit Doctor MCP server, which provides ready-made calculators for Etsy, Shopify and Amazon fees, discounts and ad break-even.

There is nothing to host: no database and no tunnel. At the end you give Cowork one business question, and it decides which tools to use, runs them, and brings the results together into a single recommendation.

Setup

⚙️ Prerequisites

Configure your machine. Install or verify every tool before starting the lab.

1

Open PowerShell as Administrator

All commands in this lab run from PowerShell. Administrator mode avoids permission issues while installing tools and creating folders.

  1. Select Start and type PowerShell.
  2. Right-click Windows PowerShell and select Run as administrator.
  3. Select Yes in the User Account Control prompt.
What to expect: A PowerShell window opens with Administrator in the title bar.
2

Verify PowerShell version (7 or later)

WIQD requires PowerShell version 7 or later. Older Windows PowerShell (5.1) can cause commands to fail.

Verify that your PowerShell version is 7 or later:

PowerShell
pwsh --version
What to expect: The output shows PowerShell 7.x.x.

If pwsh is not recognized, install the latest PowerShell (version 7 or later):

PowerShell
winget install --id Microsoft.PowerShell --source winget

After installation, search for PowerShell from Start and verify again:

PowerShell
pwsh --version
Important: The version verification is only needed here. From step 5 onward, you will use a normal PowerShell window (not as Administrator).
3

Verify Node.js and npm

WIQD runs on Node.js, so Node.js and npm must be installed.

PowerShell
node --version
PowerShell
npm --version
What to expect: Both commands return a version number (your version may be newer).

If either command is not recognized, install Node.js LTS, then close and reopen Windows PowerShell as Administrator:

PowerShell
winget install --id OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS -e
4

Verify Work IQ Dev Tools (WIQD)

WIQD creates, configures, provisions, and packages the Cowork plugin.

PowerShell
wiqd --version
What to expect: A version number is returned.

If WIQD is not recognized, install it, then reopen Windows PowerShell as Administrator:

PowerShell
iex "& { $(irm 'https://aka.ms/wiqd/install.ps1') }"
Terminal

🛠️ Build the plugin with WIQD

Open a normal PowerShell window (not as Administrator) and run all the steps below in it.

5

Create the demo folder

A clean folder keeps this plugin separate from your other labs.

Before you start: Select Start, type PowerShell and open it normally (do not choose Run as administrator). Run all the remaining steps in this window.
PowerShell
cd C:\
View reference output
PowerShell
mkdir seller-profit-demo
View reference output
PowerShell
cd seller-profit-demo
View reference output
What to expect: Your prompt shows C:\seller-profit-demo>.
6

Create the plugin project

WIQD generates the plugin structure, including manifest.json and the lifecycle files.

PowerShell
wiqd plugin create --name seller-profit-demo
View reference output
PowerShell
cd seller-profit-demo
View reference output
What to expect: Your prompt shows C:\seller-profit-demo\seller-profit-demo>.
7

Add the skill

The skill holds the instructions Cowork follows when it analyses seller profitability.

PowerShell
wiqd plugin add skill --name "seller-profit-analysis"
View reference output
What to expect: WIQD creates appPackage\skills\seller-profit-analysis\SKILL.md.
8

Write SKILL.md

This tells Cowork how to break a business question into smaller questions, which tools to use, and how to shape the answer.

PowerShell
notepad .\appPackage\skills\seller-profit-analysis\SKILL.md

Replace everything in the file with the content below, then save and close Notepad.

Markdown
---
name: seller-profit-analysis
description: Analyze ecommerce profitability, marketplace fees, discounts, advertising break-even, shipping costs and margins for Etsy, Shopify and Amazon sellers.
---

# Seller Profit Analysis

Help ecommerce sellers understand the financial impact of pricing, marketplace fees, discounts, shipping, advertising and operating costs.

Use the available Seller Profit Doctor tools when the user asks about:

- Etsy, Shopify or Amazon fees
- Profit or margin on a sale
- Marketplace comparisons
- Discounts and promotions
- Advertising break-even
- ROAS
- Shipping costs
- Pricing decisions
- Seller profitability

## Core instructions

1. Understand the seller's overall business objective before selecting a tool.
2. Break broad business questions into relevant profitability questions.
3. Determine which available tools can provide evidence for each question.
4. Use multiple tools when necessary instead of relying on one calculation.
5. Use the user's actual numbers whenever they are provided.
6. Never invent missing prices, costs, fees, order volumes, shipping costs or advertising spend.
7. Ask only for information that is essential to completing the analysis.
8. Clearly distinguish revenue, marketplace fees, operating costs and profit.
9. Explain what the calculated numbers mean in simple business language.
10. Identify the important trade-offs between different options.
11. Clearly state assumptions and defaults used by the tools.
12. Treat calculations as estimates based on the information and rates returned by the tools.

## Decision-making guidance

When the user asks a broad business question:

1. Identify the decisions the seller is trying to make.
2. Break the objective into smaller analytical questions.
3. Select the appropriate seller tools for each question.
4. Use more than one tool when the decision involves multiple factors.
5. Compare and connect the tool results.
6. Identify risks, opportunities and important trade-offs.
7. Produce one overall recommendation supported by the calculations.
8. Do not merely repeat individual tool outputs.
9. Turn the results into practical, actionable business guidance.
10. Prioritize actions according to their likely effect on profitability.

## Relevant considerations

When appropriate, consider:

- Selling price
- Shipping charged to the customer
- Marketplace fees
- Product or materials cost
- Shipping-label cost
- Packaging cost
- Discount percentage
- Current monthly order volume
- Additional orders required
- Advertising spend
- ROAS
- Break-even ROAS
- Profit per order
- Profit margin
- Monthly platform-plan fees
- Marketplace reach and marketing requirements

## Marketplace comparisons

When comparing Etsy, Shopify and Amazon:

1. Compare the fees on an equivalent sale.
2. Consider applicable monthly plan fees.
3. Consider the seller's expected monthly order volume.
4. Explain that lower transaction fees do not automatically make a platform the best business choice.
5. Consider that Etsy and Amazon may provide marketplace traffic, while Shopify may require separate marketing investment.
6. Clearly identify any assumed marketplace category, plan or advertising setting.

## Discounts

When analyzing a promotion or discount:

1. Calculate the financial effect of the discount.
2. Determine the additional orders needed to maintain the original profit.
3. Explain whether the required increase in sales appears realistic.
4. Warn the user if the discounted order produces little or no profit.
5. Recommend a smaller discount or another strategy when appropriate.

## Advertising

When analyzing advertising:

1. Calculate the seller's break-even ROAS.
2. Compare it with any actual ROAS supplied by the user.
3. Explain whether the advertising is generating or losing money.
4. Distinguish advertising-platform attribution from the seller's actual order data.
5. Avoid recommending additional advertising spend unless the available calculations support it.

## Response style

Keep answers clear, concise and business-friendly.

For broad business questions, structure the response as:

1. Executive recommendation
2. Current position
3. Options analyzed
4. Important calculations
5. Risks and assumptions
6. Recommended next actions

Use a small comparison table when it improves readability.

Always show the numbers supporting the recommendation.

Do not present the answer as a raw calculator response. Synthesize the available tool results into one decision-oriented recommendation.
View reference output
What to expect: The name in the file matches the folder name: seller-profit-analysis.

10

Save toolDescription.json as UTF-8

Notepad can save the file in a way the package validator rejects. This re-saves it as plain UTF-8.

PowerShell
$json = Get-Content .\appPackage\toolDescription.json -Raw
View reference output
PowerShell
[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText((Resolve-Path .\appPackage\toolDescription.json),$json,[System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false))
View reference output
What to expect: Both commands finish with no output.
11

Add the Seller Profit Doctor connector

The connector links the plugin to the public Seller Profit Doctor MCP server.

PowerShell
wiqd plugin add connector --name "Seller Profit Doctor" --description "Read-only seller profitability tools for Etsy, Shopify and Amazon" --url "https://sellerprofitdoctor.com/api/mcp" --tool-description ./toolDescription.json
View reference output
What to expect: Added MCP connector "Seller Profit Doctor" with Auth None.
12

Validate the project

A quick offline verification of the project before it is registered.

PowerShell
wiqd plugin validate --mode source --env dev
View reference output
What to expect: Validation shows PASSED.
13

Sign in to WIQD

WIQD needs your Microsoft 365 account to register the plugin.

PowerShell
wiqd auth login --interactive
  1. Choose Discover my sign-in directory.
  2. Pick your lab account and select Continue.
View reference output
View reference output
View reference output
Note: A Partner Center (Marketplace) check failure can be ignored for this lab. Only the Microsoft 365 sign-in matters.

17

Ask Cowork a business question

Instead of naming a tool, give Cowork a goal. It splits the goal into smaller questions, picks the right tools, and joins the results into one recommendation.

Start a new Cowork task and enter this prompt:

Prompt
I run a small online business selling a product for $50. My product costs me $15, shipping costs $6, packaging costs $2, and I charge customers $5 for shipping. I currently sell about 30 units a month on Etsy.

I'm considering offering a 20% discount to grow sales. I'm also evaluating whether Shopify or Amazon would be more profitable, and whether I should spend $500 a month on Facebook and Instagram advertising.

Act as my profitability advisor. Analyze my current position and these options. Use the available seller tools where relevant, connect the findings, identify the important trade-offs, and recommend what I should do to improve profitability.

Show the calculations supporting your recommendation, clearly state any assumptions, and give me a prioritized action plan. Do not treat each calculation as a separate answer. Give me one overall business recommendation.
View reference output
View reference output
Note: These tools only calculate and change nothing, so Cowork runs them without asking for approval.
What to expect: One recommendation covering the current Etsy profit, the 20% discount, Shopify and Amazon, and the $500 ad budget, with the numbers and assumptions behind it.
